title: Beer Hall Putsch
summary: On the night of 8 November 1923 Hitler and the Kampfbund seized a political meeting in a Munich beer hall and declared a national revolution; the march on the Feldherrnhalle the next morning was stopped by police fire that killed sixteen of the marchers and four policemen. It failed completely, and it was the making of the party that attempted it: the trial gave Hitler a national platform, the sentence was five years of which he served nine months, and the lesson he drew — that power would have to be taken legally and then used — is the strategy of 1933. It is in the atlas as the point at which the Weimar Republic's most dangerous enemy learned how to beat it.
